Class GameController

java.lang.Object
com.tetris.gameLogic.GameController
All Implemented Interfaces:
InputEventListener
public class GameController extends Object implements InputEventListener
The central controller for the Tetris game application.

This class implements the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern by acting as the intermediary between the Board (Model) and the GameView (View). It is responsible for:

  • Managing the main game loop (JavaFX Timeline).
  • Processing user inputs (keyboard events).
  • Coordinating game states (Pause, Freeze, Game Over).
  • Updating the score, levels, and playing sounds.
Author:
Jacob Villegas

  • Constructor Details

    • GameController

      public GameController(GameView view)
      Constructs a new GameController and initializes the game environment.

      This sets up the UI bindings for scores and levels, loads high scores, initializes the starting board state, and starts the background music.

      Parameters:
      view - The UI view responsible for rendering the game.

  • Method Details

    • createGameLoop

      private javafx.animation.Timeline createGameLoop()
      Creates the main game loop using a JavaFX Timeline.

      The loop triggers on every tick (determined by the current level speed). If the game is not currently "Frozen", it forces a Move Down event.

      Returns:
      A configured Timeline object.

    • updateGameLoop

      private void updateGameLoop()
      Recreates and restarts the game loop to apply new speed settings.

      This is called whenever the player levels up to make the game faster.

    • handleIntersect

      private DownData handleIntersect()
      Processes logic when a brick hits the bottom or another piece.

      This method:

      1. Plays the drop sound.
      2. Merges the brick into the board matrix.
      3. Checks for and processes cleared lines.
      4. Checks for Game Over conditions.
      5. Refreshes the view.
      Returns:
      The data required to update the UI (cleared lines, score, etc).
